name: prose-review
description: Two read-only critics and one revising transformer for prose: does this draft sound like its author, did a revision keep what it had to, and apply a plan of edits under a fidelity gate.

interface.shortDescription: Critics that judge a draft against the author's own writing, plus a reviser that applies a plan under a fidelity gate.
interface.longDescription: Two read-only critics and one revising transformer, each owning one question exclusively. prose-voice-critic: whether a draft sounds like the person it is supposed to be by, judged against a corpus of their own writing, with every finding required to cite how they write instead. prose-fidelity-critic: whether a revision kept the facts, quotes, named entities, qualifications and claim strength of the original, judged against a deterministic scan that is authoritative on presence so the critic argues only about consequence. prose-reviser: takes an ORIGINAL and an edit PLAN and emits a change log the harness applies, then the fidelity critic judges — the reviser cannot make out-of-plan edits by construction because its only output channel is a list of before/after pairs referring to plan ids. Neither critic judges quality, and none of these primitives state or imply that text was machine-generated. NOTE: Codex enforces neither the read-only tool restriction nor context isolation. Run each as a fresh `codex exec` rather than inline, and route the reviser's log through the fidelity gate before saving the reconstructed revision — the shape of the safety here is the gate, not the prompt. See docs/portability.md.
defaultPrompt: Does this draft sound like me?
Review this against my writing corpus for voice
Which passages here do not match how I write?
Did this rewrite drop anything from the original?
Apply this plan of edits to the draft
Revise this section under the fidelity gate
